I can't tell you whether to buy or keep renting. That depends on your finances, goals and risk tolerance, which is personal advice outside what I can give. I can share one relevant Statistics Canada figure, but it doesn't settle the question.

What I found: Statistics Canada's New Housing Price Index for the Toronto census metropolitan area (total, house and land) fell from 110.4 in 2025-09 to 105.0 in 2026-09. That is a change of (105.0 − 110.4) / 110.4 = −4.9% over 12 months. This covers newly built homes only, not resale homes, so it doesn't show what a typical Toronto buyer would pay.

What I could not get: I did not retrieve a Toronto rent series, so I can't compare rent with ownership costs. I also have no mortgage-rate, resale-price or income data in this session. For a buy-versus-rent comparison, you could look at the Consumer Price Index tables (18-10-0004 for Toronto rent components) and the residential property price tables on the StatCan site, and pair them with current mortgage rates from your lender.
